UP-Term kit: parts, licences and where the source is

Every part the kit (up-term.lha) ships is listed once. The source column
names the repository (all side by side in one workspace directory, pinned together by the upterm
meta-repo, repos.lock) or the archive the source is in. "unconfirmed" means
no licence file or statement for it was found in the tree; the place looked
is named.

Notes
- GNU Unifont is also offered under GPL v2 or later; the kit uses the OFL.
- Source for the GPL parts is in the kit as source archives where the table
  says so, or in up-term-src.lha; for GNU screen and tmux it is in the
  repositories named, which the upterm meta-repo pins to the commits the kit
  was built from.
- Claude, amiga-pi, Python and Neovim are archives of their own
  (up-claude.lha, up-pi.lha, up-python.lha, up-nvim.lha),
  each with its own LICENSES.txt. Git, Perl, Vim, BitchX and vbcc are upkg
  packages (upkg install git, perl, vim, bitchx, vbcc): their licence files and SOURCES rows are in
  UP-Term:licenses once installed, as the base had them.
